record.original_question: Do local symplectic invariants exist for diffeomorphic dege nerate singularities? How many and of what kind are they? This question makes sense even in the simplest case of one-degree- of-freedom systems. As we know from concrete examples of integrable systems, many de generate singularities are stable in the sense that they cannot be destroyed by a small perturbatio n of the system [25, 85, 124]. The problem of description of stable degenerate singularities is very impo rtant on its own right, but for many degrees of freedom, it is quite complicated. However, in the ca se of two degrees of freedom (perhaps depending on a parameter), there is a number of well-kno wn examples of stable bifurcations (e.g., integrable period-doubling [25] and Hamiltonian Hopf bifurcation [70]). It would be interesting to clarify the situation with asymptotic behaviour of angle variables a t least for them. V. Kalashnikov [124] has described all stable singularities of rank 1 fo r Hamiltonian systems of two degrees of freedom.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold and let $F=(f_1,\dots,f_n)\colon M\to\mathbb{R}^n$ be the momentum map of a completely integrable Hamiltonian system, i.e. the functions $f_1,\dots,f_n$ are smooth, functionally independent on an open dense subset, and pairwise Poisson-commuting with respect to $\omega$. A point $p\in M$ is a singular point of $F$ if $\mathrm{rank}\,dF(p)<n$, and it is called degenerate if the linearization of the system at $p$ does not satisfy the Williamson non-degeneracy condition (so that Eliasson's symplectic linearization theorem does not apply). Two singularities $(F,p)$ and $(F',p')$ are diffeomorphic (or fibrewise topologically equivalent) if there is a local diffeomorphism of neighbourhoods sending the level sets of $F$ to those of $F'$ and $p$ to $p'$; they are symplectically equivalent if this diffeomorphism can be chosen to be a symplectomorphism that intertwines the foliations defined by $F$ and $F'$.

(a) Do there exist local symplectic invariants distinguishing diffeomorphic but symplectically inequivalent degenerate singularities of integrable Hamiltonian systems? In other words, can two degenerate singularities be topologically (fibrewise) equivalent yet fail to be symplectically equivalent?

(b) If such invariants exist, describe their nature, classify them, and determine how many independent invariants are needed in the case of one degree of freedom ($n=1$), and in the case of two degrees of freedom ($n=2$), including families depending on a parameter and the stable bifurcation types such as the integrable period-doubling bifurcation and the Hamiltonian Hopf bifurcation. In particular, clarify the asymptotic behaviour of the action–angle variables near such stable degenerate singularities.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question remains open, but partial progress has been made. Bolsinov, Guglielmi and Kudryavtseva (2018) and follow-up work (e.g. arXiv:2110.13758, 2023) have constructed local symplectic invariants for parabolic orbits and cusp singularities of integrable systems with two degrees of freedom; a 2025 Regular and Chaotic Dynamics paper gives a symplectic classification for universal unfoldings of $A_n$ singularities. Kalashnikov's classification of stable rank-1 singularities for two-degree-of-freedom systems is known, but a general classification of symplectic invariants for arbitrary degenerate singularities (and the asymptotics of angle variables near them) is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic invariants for parabolic orbits and cusp singularities of integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: We construct symplectic invariants for parabolic orbits and cusp singularities of integrable Hamiltonian systems with two degrees of freedom.
status_evidence.claim: Symplectic invariants have been constructed for specific degenerate singularities (parabolic orbits, cusps) in two degrees of freedom, providing partial answers.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic Classification for Universal Unfoldings of A_n Singularities in Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Symplectic classification of universal unfoldings of A_n singularities in integrable Hamiltonian systems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) work classifies symplectic invariants for A_n-type degenerate singularities, further partial progress.

status_evidence.title: C∞ Symplectic Invariants of Parabolic Orbits and Flaps in Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth symplectic invariants for parabolic orbits and flaps in integrable systems.
status_evidence.claim: Provides further smooth symplectic invariants for degenerate singularities of two-degree-of-freedom integrable systems.

status_evidence.title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems, including symplectic invariants of degenerate singularities.
status_evidence.claim: The general problem of local symplectic invariants for degenerate singularities is stated as an open problem.
